I read the Rsubread users guide and learning that "When counting
reads to meta-features (eg. genes) columns `Chr', `Start', `End' and `Strand' may each contain

in the same meta-feature."

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: featurecounts contain multiple values in Chr, Start, End and Strand
parts:
The 'Length' column gives the effective length of each gene, which is the total number of unique bases in exons that belong to the gene.

Regarding the output from meta-feature level counting, featureCounts has to output chr names for each exon because of the possibility that some genes are located on more than one chromosome. It is not hard to reduce these chr names to unique names:

> unlist(lapply(strsplit(c("Chr01;Chr01;Chr01;Chr01;Chr01", "Chr02;Chr02;Chr02"),';'),unique))
[1] "Chr01" "Chr02"

Hi Wei,

Thank you!

Regarding the featureCounts has to output chr names for each exon because of the possibility that some genes are located on more than one chromosome, don't is more easy to down application analysis if these output are put in separately? For example:

Eucgr.C00550.chr01 .......
Eucgr.C00550.chr11 .......

In your example:

GeneXXX.Chr01    5
GeneXXX.Chr02    3

This generate a unique ID and is straightforward for detect if isoform or ontolog is DE.

Thanks

Laia ML

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: featurecounts contain multiple values in Chr, Start, End and Strand
parts: I am not quite sure what you mean here. But featureCounts is not intended for the isoform or ortholog analysis. featureCounts uses the same gene ids as provided in the GTF file and it does not change them.
